name: MathlibAnnex.WeakDivergenceZero.nonempty_localAEConstantAt
title: Local almost-everywhere constancy from the weak equation

content.display_title: Local almost-everywhere constancy from the weak equation
content.one_sentence_role: Turns constant mollifications into one almost-everywhere constant by choosing a common convergence point.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real normed vector space with its Borel structure and an additive Haar measure $\mu$. Let $U\subseteq E$ be open and $u:E\to\mathbb R$ locally integrable on $U$. Assume
$$\int_Uu(z)\operatorname{div}W(z)\,d\mu(z)=0$$
for every $C^1$ vector field $W:E\to E$ for which a compact set $K_W$ satisfies
$$\overline{\{z\in E:W(z)\ne0\}}\subseteq K_W\subseteq U.$$
Here $\operatorname{div}W(z):=\operatorname{tr}(DW(z))$. For every $x\in U$, there are an open set $V$ and a real number $c$ with
$$x\in V\subseteq U,\qquad u=c\quad\mu|_V\text{-almost everywhere}.$$
content.assumptions: The domain need not be connected, bounded, or of finite measure. There is no global integrability, Lipschitz, or continuity assumption on $u$. No positive-dimension hypothesis is imposed. A point $x\in U$ is supplied, so the conclusion is local; if $U$ is empty, there is no such point to consider.
content.conclusion: The conclusion provides an open neighborhood $V$ of the prescribed point $x$, with $V\subseteq U$, and a real constant $c$ such that $u=c$ almost everywhere on $V$. It does not assert $u(x)=c$ at the originally supplied point, which might be exceptional.
content.proof_summary: Localize to a compact ball. The weak equation makes every derivative of each smooth mollification zero on the inner ball, hence each mollification is constant there. Almost-everywhere convergence at one fixed good point forces these constants to converge. Uniqueness of limits then identifies the value at almost every other point.

proof_steps.text:
**Choose a compact localization.** [The local-ball existence lemma](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Distribution/WeakGradient/Local.lean#L88-L101), applied to openness at $x$, permits choosing $R>0$ with $\overline B(x,4R)\subseteq U$. Put
$$B:=B(x,R),\qquad K:=\overline B(x,4R),\qquad
v(z):=\begin{cases}u(z),&z\in K,\\0,&z\notin K.\end{cases}$$
The inner ball is open, contains $x$, and lies in $K\subseteq U$. The closed ball $K$ is compact and measurable. Local integrability on $U$ gives integrability on $K$, so $v$ is globally integrable and therefore locally integrable on $E$. In particular $v=u$ on $B$, also almost everywhere for $\mu|_B$.

**Use one shrinking sequence of kernels.** Choose normalized smooth bumps $\varphi_k$ centered at zero with inner radius $a_k=R/(2(k+2))$ and outer radius $r_k=R/(k+2)$. In particular,
$$\varphi_k\ge0,\qquad\int_E\varphi_k\,d\mu=1,\qquad
\overline{\{z:\varphi_k(z)\ne0\}}\subseteq\overline B(0,r_k).$$
$$v_k(y):=\int_E\varphi_k(t)v(y-t)\,d\mu(t).$$
These functions are smooth by the compact-kernel convolution theorem. The radii satisfy $r_k\to0$ and $r_k=2a_k$. [The normalized-bump convergence theorem for locally integrable functions](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Distribution/WeakGradient/Local.lean#L200-L211) therefore gives
$$v_k(y)\longrightarrow v(y)\qquad\text{for }\mu\text{-almost every }y.$$
The hypotheses are precisely local integrability of $v$, shrinking outer radii, and a uniform bound $2$ on the ratio of outer to inner radius.

**Make every mollification constant on the inner ball.** Apply [the vanishing-directional-derivative theorem](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Distribution/WeakGradient/Local.lean#L353-L373) to this open $U$, this local ball data, the given local integrability, and the weak equation. It gives
$$Dv_k(y)e=0\qquad(y\in B,\ e\in E).$$
Thus $Dv_k(y)$ is the zero linear functional. The ball $B$ is convex, hence preconnected, and $v_k$ is differentiable there. Thus [the constancy theorem for each local mollification](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Distribution/WeakGradient/Local.lean#L402-L416) applies; its proof uses zero-derivative constancy on the open preconnected ball and supplies a real number $c_k$ such that
$$v_k(y)=c_k\qquad\text{for every }y\in B.$$
This is pointwise constancy of each smooth mollification, not yet a statement about the limit $u$.

**Choose a single point at which the whole sequence converges.** The nonempty open ball has positive Haar measure. Restrict the almost-everywhere convergence in Step 2 to $B$ and intersect it with almost-everywhere membership in the measurable set $B$. [The inner-ball convergence-point lemma](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Distribution/WeakGradient/Local.lean#L424-L451) therefore supplies one $y_0\in B$ at which the entire sequence converges. Set $c=v(y_0)$. Then
$$c_k=v_k(y_0)\longrightarrow v(y_0)=c.$$
This fixed good point is the reason the constants converge. We neither assume that $(c_k)$ converges nor choose a different exceptional-set witness for each $k$.

**Pass to almost every other point and undo localization.** For almost every $y$ with respect to $\mu|_B$, Step 2 gives $v_k(y)\to v(y)$ and $y\in B$. Step 3 gives $v_k(y)=c_k=v_k(y_0)$ for every $k$. Step 4 and uniqueness of real limits therefore imply
$$v(y)=\lim_{k\to\infty}v_k(y)=\lim_{k\to\infty}c_k=c.$$
Since $v=u$ on $B$, this gives $u=c$ almost everywhere for $\mu|_B$. Taking $V=B$ supplies all the promised local data.

content.lean_realization_notes: The construction below uses the inner ball $B(x,R)$, the compact carrier $K=\overline B(x,4R)$, and the intermediate ball $\overline B(x,2R)$. All inclusions and compactness assertions follow from the chosen ball data and finite dimensionality. The same localized function and the same kernel sequence are used throughout.
